title: Verify an audit-enabled Linux live watchpoint
changes: Record one live synthetic write watch and matched execution control using an existing audit-feature interpreter.
validation: A derived public synthetic ROM executed ARM instructions that wrote 91 to 0x02000000. An audit-enabled debug-control watch reported the four-byte write after the complete interpreter step; read-only inspection confirmed the backing bytes. A separate copy stopped at the next instruction without a watch and matched the full guest-state hash, clock, registers, keys and pause state. Both windows closed normally and declared inputs remained protected (dbg27-linux-live-watch-final-dq5hpsy0).

The first fixture used a seed bound to a different ROM and was refused before execution (xl2p7po4). A subsequent boot run passed but copied an unused seed outside the declared protection list (y_1grav5); the final proof removed that dependency and guarded all inputs.
limitations: This verifies one synthetic ARM write via local control on Linux/Xvfb using an existing feature-enabled executable SHA-256 c3609dfe9017ca7d1424f5850e6e3e988bb54c3d709ff289177b1b2f9ee466e5, not current-source rebuild equivalence, other watch types or sites, physical controller, native Windows, or every command channel.
